Quicksort in a nutshell

Quicksort picks a pivot, partitions the list, and recurses. See the overview for details.

  • Average time: O(n log n)
  • Worst case:
    • Already sorted input with a bad pivot
    • All keys equal
  1. Third step
  2. Fourth step
python
def quicksort(items):
    if len(items) <= 1:
        return items
    pivot, *rest = items
    return quicksort([x for x in rest if x < pivot]) + [pivot] + quicksort([x for x in rest if x >= pivot])
AlgorithmAverageStable?
QuicksortO(n log n)No
Merge sortO(n log n)Yes

The expected cost is T(n)T(n) = 2T(n/2) + nT(n)=2T(n/2)+n, which solves to:

TT(n) = \Theta(n \log n)T(n)=Θ(n log n)

Pick the pivot randomly to avoid the worst case.
